0.long_answer: Medications used to treat cardiomyopathy caused by wild‐type or variant transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis, such as acoramidis (Attruby), have been associated with gastrointestinal side effects. Clinical studies have consistently reported that the most common adverse reactions include diarrhea and upper abdominal pain. These side effects are generally mild and are a result of the medication’s impact on the gastrointestinal system. Although additional side effects such as general pain have been noted in some cases, the primary and most frequently observed effects remain diarrhea and upper abdominal pain.
